title: Wipeout 3
subtitle: A future drawn with restraint

body: Wipeout 3 is Psygnosis Leeds' PlayStation anti-gravity racing game, first released in Europe on 10 September 1999. Fast craft compete on futuristic circuits, using airbrakes, speed pads and weapons to manage both the route and the opposition. The Designers Republic helped give the game a restrained visual identity, extending a consistent language from menus to the racing world. Clean presentation supports an activity that quickly becomes demanding. The player must see the approaching turn, choose a line and make the craft follow it before the next wall arrives.

Steering an anti-gravity craft means allowing for its movement across the track rather than treating it like a car fixed to the road. Airbrakes tighten the approach to corners, while pickups add decisions about attack and defence. A small error can interrupt a promising lap, making practice on a familiar circuit valuable. Learning where to brake and where the course opens out gives speed a deliberate shape. The challenge comes from maintaining that rhythm while other craft and weapons introduce problems that cannot be solved by memorising the road alone.

DJ Sasha selected an electronic soundtrack that includes Orbital and The Chemical Brothers, linking the racing atmosphere to contemporary club music. The game also supported widescreen and a high-resolution mode on the original PlayStation. Reviewers praised its graphics, music and minimalist presentation while noting its demanding difficulty. A European Special Edition in 2000 added further courses and content. As the last Wipeout on the first PlayStation, it brings that console's version of the series to a visually coherent conclusion before Wipeout Fusion moved to PlayStation 2.
